instructions: Negative Marking: 1/3 mark deducted for wrong 1-mark MCQ, 2/3 mark for wrong 2-mark MCQ.
NO negative marking for MSQ or NAT questions.

questions.question:
The table below shows the quantity of paddy (in tonnes) procured by a State Agricultural Marketing Board from four districts in two consecutive years.
Which district recorded the highest percentage increase in procurement from Year 1 to Year 2?

options.A: P
options.B: Q
options.D: S

questions.solution:
Percentage increase = (Year2 − Year1)/Year1 × 100.
P: (480−420)/420×100 = 14.29%
Q: (700−650)/650×100 = 7.69%
R: (375−300)/300×100 = 25.00%
S: (580−540)/540×100 = 7.41%
R has the highest percentage increase (25.00%), so (C) is correct.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) 14.29% increase — smaller than R's.
(B) 7.69% increase — a modest gain relative to base, not the highest.
(D) 7.41% increase — the lowest percentage rise among the four.

questions.question: Select the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'meticulous'.

options.A: Careless
options.B: Diligent
options.D: Thorough

questions.solution:
'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. Its opposite is 'careless', meaning lacking attention or thoroughness.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) 'Diligent' is a near-synonym of meticulous, not an antonym.
(C) 'Precise' is itself close in meaning to meticulous.
(D) 'Thorough' is also a synonym, not an antonym.

questions.question: Five farms P, Q, R, S and T lie in a row from left to right along a canal. Q is at the left end. R is immediately to the right of Q. T is at the right (last) end. S is immediately to the left of T. What is the position of P counted from the left end?

options.A: 1st
options.B: 2nd
options.D: 4th

questions.solution:
Q is at position 1 (left end). R is immediately right of Q, so R is at position 2. T is at position 5 (right end). S is immediately left of T, so S is at position 4. The only remaining position, 3, must be occupied by P. Hence P is 3rd from the left.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Position 1 is occupied by Q.
(B) Position 2 is occupied by R.
(D) Position 4 is occupied by S.

questions.question: A farmer sells 60% of his wheat stock and still has 140 quintals left. What was the original stock (in quintals)?
questions.solution:
If original stock = x, remaining after selling 60% = 40% of x = 140.
x = 140/0.40 = 350 quintals.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Would correspond to 50% of stock remaining, not 40%.
(B) Does not satisfy 0.4x = 140.
(D) Corresponds to 35% of stock remaining, not the given 40%.

questions.question: The ratio of the ages of a tractor and a power tiller owned by a farm is 5:3. Four years ago, the ratio was 3:1. What is the present age of the tractor (in years)?
questions.solution:
Let present ages be 5x and 3x. Four years ago: (5x−4)/(3x−4) = 3/1.
5x − 4 = 9x − 12 → 4x = 8 → x = 2.
Present age of tractor = 5x = 10 years.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Corresponds to x = 1.2, which does not satisfy the ratio equation.
(B) Corresponds to x = 1.6, inconsistent with the four-years-ago ratio.
(D) Corresponds to x = 2.4, which fails the given past ratio.

questions.question: [Figure description: A square sheet of paper is folded in half vertically (left half over right half), then folded again in half horizontally (top half over bottom half), giving a smaller square one-quarter the original area. A single small circular hole is then punched through all layers at a point strictly inside the folded square, away from both fold edges.] When the paper is fully unfolded, how many holes appear on the sheet, and what is their arrangement?

options.A: 1 hole, at the exact centre of the sheet
options.B: 2 holes, symmetric about the vertical fold line only
options.C: 4 holes, one in each quadrant, symmetric about both fold lines
options.D: 4 holes, arranged along a single diagonal

questions.solution:
Two perpendicular folds (vertical then horizontal) create four layers of paper stacked together. A hole punched away from both fold lines passes through all four layers, so unfolding reproduces the hole once in each of the four quadrants, positioned as mirror images of one another about both the vertical and horizontal fold lines.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) A single hole would result only if the punch fell exactly on both fold lines (the true centre), not at an interior quadrant point.
(B) Two holes would result from only a single fold, not two perpendicular folds.
(D) The four holes are symmetric about both axes; they need not lie on one diagonal.

questions.question:
Read the following statements and identify the option that presents them in the most logically coherent order.
P: As a result, post-harvest losses in perishable produce fell sharply.
Q: A national cold-chain infrastructure programme was launched in 2015.
R: The programme financed refrigerated transport and pack-houses near farm clusters.
S: This reduced the time between harvest and cold storage for fruits and vegetables.

options.A: Q, R, S, P
options.B: Q, P, R, S
options.D: Q, S, R, P

questions.solution:
The logical chain is: the programme was launched (Q) → it financed specific infrastructure (R) → this reduced the harvest-to-storage time (S) → which in turn cut post-harvest losses (P). The coherent order is Q, R, S, P.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Places the outcome (P) before the enabling infrastructure (R) and its consequence (S), breaking the cause-effect chain.
(C) Opens with R, a detail of the programme, before introducing the programme itself (Q).
(D) Places S before R, but the reduced storage time (S) is a direct result of the infrastructure (R), which must come first.

questions.question:
Statement: 'All soils that are well-drained are suitable for groundnut cultivation. Some red soils are well-drained.'
Which of the following conclusions necessarily follows?

options.A: All red soils are suitable for groundnut cultivation
options.B: Some red soils are suitable for groundnut cultivation
options.C: No red soils are suitable for groundnut cultivation
options.D: All soils suitable for groundnut cultivation are red soils

questions.solution:
Since some red soils are well-drained, and all well-drained soils are suitable for groundnut, at least those (some) red soils must be suitable for groundnut cultivation. This is a valid 'some' conclusion by syllogism.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Overstates the conclusion — only 'some', not 'all', red soils are known to be well-drained.
(C) Directly contradicts the valid 'some' conclusion.
(D) Reverses the logical direction; well-drained soils being suitable does not imply all suitable soils are red.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill an irrigation storage tank in 12 hours, and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Both pipes are opened together, but Pipe B is shut after 4 hours. In how many more hours will Pipe A alone fill the remaining tank?
questions.solution:
Rate of A = 1/12 tank/hr, rate of B = 1/15 tank/hr.
In 4 hours together: 4 × (1/12 + 1/15) = 4 × (5/60 + 4/60) = 4 × (9/60) = 36/60 = 0.6 tank filled.
Remaining tank = 1 − 0.6 = 0.4.
Time for A alone to fill 0.4 tank = 0.4 ÷ (1/12) = 0.4 × 12 = 4.8 hours.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Results from using the combined rate instead of A's individual rate for the remaining portion.
(B) Results from an arithmetic slip while combining the two rates over 4 hours.
(D) Results from mis-subtracting the joint-filling contribution from the full tank.

questions.question: A committee of 4 members is to be selected from 6 agricultural engineers and 5 soil scientists such that the committee has at least 2 soil scientists. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.solution:
At least 2 soil scientists (SS) out of 4 members: possible splits are (2 SS, 2 AE), (3 SS, 1 AE), (4 SS, 0 AE).
C(5,2)×C(6,2) = 10×15 = 150
C(5,3)×C(6,1) = 10×6 = 60
C(5,4)×C(6,0) = 5×1 = 5
Total = 150 + 60 + 5 = 215.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Undercounts by omitting part of the all-soil-scientist or 3–1 case.
(B) Results from a combinatorial slip in one of the three cases.
(D) Overcounts by including an invalid selection combination.

questions.question: Evaluate: lim (x→0) (e^{2x} − 1) / x

options.D: 2e

questions.solution:
Using the standard limit lim(x→0) (e^{kx}−1)/x = k (from the series e^{kx} = 1 + kx + (kx)²/2! + ...), with k = 2, the limit equals 2.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Corresponds to k = 1, not the given k = 2 in the exponent.
(C) Confuses the limit value with the base of the natural exponential.
(D) Results from doubling the correct answer by mistake, e.g. multiplying by e unnecessarily.

questions.question: The function f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 2 has a local minimum at x = ?
questions.solution:
f'(x) = 3x² − 6x = 3x(x−2) = 0 gives critical points x = 0, 2.
f''(x) = 6x − 6.
At x = 0: f''(0) = −6 < 0 → local maximum.
At x = 2: f''(2) = 6 > 0 → local minimum.
Hence the local minimum is at x = 2.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) x = 0 is a local maximum (f''(0) < 0), not a minimum.
(B) x = 1 is not a critical point since f'(1) = 3 − 6 = −3 ≠ 0.
(D) x = 3 is not a critical point since f'(3) = 27 − 18 = 9 ≠ 0.

questions.question: For a function f(x, y) with continuous second-order partial derivatives in a neighbourhood of a point, the mixed partial derivatives ∂²f/∂x∂y and ∂²f/∂y∂x at that point are:

options.A: Always equal
options.B: Always unequal
options.C: Equal only if f is linear in x and y
options.D: Equal only at critical points of f

questions.solution:
By Schwarz's (Clairaut's) theorem, if the mixed second-order partial derivatives of f are continuous at a point, then ∂²f/∂x∂y = ∂²f/∂y∂x at that point, regardless of the specific form of f.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Contradicts Schwarz's theorem, which guarantees equality under continuity.
(C) The equality holds generally under the continuity condition, not only for linear functions.
(D) The equality is a consequence of continuity of the mixed partials, unrelated to critical points.

questions.question: What are the order and degree, respectively, of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx) = x⁵ ?
questions.solution:
The order is the highest derivative present, which is d²y/dx² → order 2. The degree is the power to which the highest-order derivative is raised (after the equation is made a polynomial in derivatives), which here is 3. So (order, degree) = (2, 3).
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Swaps the order and degree values.
(C) Correctly identifies the order (2) but understates the degree (the cube on the highest derivative gives degree 3, not 2).
(D) Overstates the order; the highest derivative is second-order, not third.

questions.question: Which solution method is most directly applicable to dy/dx + (2/x) y = x³ ?

options.A: Separation of variables
options.B: Integrating factor (linear first-order method)
options.C: Solving directly as an exact equation without modification
options.D: Homogeneous-equation substitution y = vx

questions.solution:
The equation has the form dy/dx + P(x) y = Q(x) with P(x) = 2/x and Q(x) = x³, which is a linear first-order ODE. The standard method is to compute the integrating factor IF = e^{∫P dx} = e^{2 ln x} = x², multiply through, and integrate.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) The variables x and y cannot be separated because of the y/x coupling term.
(C) In its given form M dx + N dy = 0 is not exact; it must first be recast, which is exactly what the integrating factor does.
(D) The equation is not homogeneous in x and y (it is linear, not a ratio-only function of y/x).

questions.topic: Equipment for sowing, planting and fertilizer application
questions.subtopic: Equipment for sowing, planting and fertilizer application
questions.question: Which type of seed-metering mechanism is generally preferred for precision planting of large, uniformly sized seeds such as maize, where accurate single-seed spacing is required?

options.A: Fluted-roller metering
options.B: Cell-wheel (cup-feed) metering
options.D: Pneumatic (air/vacuum) plate metering

questions.solution:
Pneumatic (vacuum) metering picks up and releases exactly one seed per cell using suction, giving the highest single-seed spacing accuracy for large, uniform seeds like maize — this is why it is the standard on modern precision planters.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Fluted-roller metering is a volumetric (continuous-flow) mechanism used mainly for small grains/cereals, not precision single-seed spacing.
(B) Cell-wheel/cup-feed metering gives reasonable but lower spacing precision than vacuum metering, with more skips/doubles at higher speeds.
(C) Inclined-plate metering is an older mechanical method with lower precision and higher seed damage risk than pneumatic metering.

questions.topic: Cost analysis of implements and tractors
questions.subtopic: Cost analysis of implements and tractors
questions.question: Depreciation, interest on investment, insurance, and housing costs of a tractor are classified as:

options.A: Fixed (ownership) costs
options.B: Variable (operating) costs
options.D: Repair and maintenance costs

questions.solution:
Fixed (ownership) costs are incurred simply by owning the machine, irrespective of how much it is used — depreciation, interest, insurance, taxes, and housing/shelter all fall in this category.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Variable costs (fuel, lubricants, repairs) depend on hours of use, unlike the listed items.
(C) Labour cost is a separate operating cost category, not related to ownership.
(D) Repair and maintenance cost is a variable/operating cost that scales with usage.

questions.question: In a flat-belt drive, 'slip' refers to:

options.A: Relative motion between the belt and pulley surface that reduces the actual driven-pulley speed below the theoretical value
options.B: Permanent elongation (stretch) of the belt material with age
options.C: Angular misalignment between the driving and driven shafts
options.D: Loss of power solely due to air resistance on the moving belt

questions.solution:
Slip is the relative sliding motion between the belt and the pulley surface (due to insufficient friction/grip), which causes the driven pulley to rotate slower than the theoretical speed ratio predicts.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Belt stretch is a separate, permanent material effect, not the kinematic slip phenomenon.
(C) Shaft misalignment is a mechanical installation issue, unrelated to the belt–pulley friction definition of slip.
(D) Air resistance is a negligible, unrelated loss mechanism, not what 'slip' refers to.

questions.question: Among the following renewable energy sources used on farms, which one is most affected by seasonal and diurnal (day–night) variability, generally requiring energy storage for continuous use?

options.A: Solar photovoltaic power
options.B: Biomass gasifier power
options.D: Biogas from a continuously-fed digester

questions.solution:
Solar PV output depends directly on incident solar radiation, which varies with time of day, cloud cover, and season, making it the most intermittent of the listed sources and typically requiring battery storage for round-the-clock use.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) A biomass gasifier's fuel (biomass) can be stockpiled, so power generation is largely independent of time of day.
(C) Draft animal power is available on demand during working hours and is not tied to solar/diurnal cycles.
(D) A continuously-fed digester produces biogas at a relatively steady rate, unlike solar radiation.

questions.question: Prolonged exposure of a tractor operator to whole-body vibration during field operations is primarily associated with an increased risk of:

options.A: Lower back and spinal disorders
options.B: Hearing loss
options.D: Heat stroke

questions.solution:
Whole-body vibration transmitted through the tractor seat to the operator's spine over prolonged periods is a well-documented ergonomic hazard associated with lower back pain and spinal disorders.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Hearing loss is associated with prolonged noise exposure, not vibration.
(C) Bites are an unrelated environmental/field hazard, not a vibration effect.
(D) Heat stroke is linked to thermal/heat stress, not mechanical vibration.

questions.question: The Cetane number of a diesel fuel is a measure of:

options.A: Its ignition quality — the ease with which it self-ignites under compression
options.B: Its resistance to knocking in spark-ignition (petrol) engines
options.C: Its calorific value per unit mass
options.D: Its viscosity at low ambient temperature

questions.solution:
Cetane number rates a diesel fuel's autoignition quality: a higher Cetane number means a shorter ignition delay after injection, giving smoother combustion in a compression-ignition engine.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Knock resistance in petrol (SI) engines is rated by Octane number, the inverse-type property to Cetane number.
(C) Calorific value is a separate energy-content property, not what Cetane number measures.
(D) Low-temperature viscosity (cold-flow property) is unrelated to ignition quality.

questions.question:
A tractor gearbox has a pinion gear with 20 teeth meshing with a driven gear having 60 teeth. If the pinion rotates at 900 rpm, calculate the speed of the driven gear. (Answer in rpm.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: rpm]
questions.solution:
For meshing gears: N₁T₁ = N₂T₂
N₂ = N₁T₁/T₂ = (900 × 20)/60 = 300 rpm.

questions.question: The unit hydrograph theory for a watershed is based on the assumption that:

options.A: For a given duration, direct-runoff hydrograph ordinates are directly proportional to the volume of rainfall excess, and the base time of the hydrograph remains constant
options.B: Infiltration losses are uniform in space but vary arbitrarily with time
options.C: The hydrograph's time base changes proportionally with rainfall intensity
options.D: Baseflow is always included within the direct-runoff hydrograph ordinates

questions.solution:
The unit hydrograph treats the watershed as a linear, time-invariant system: for rainfall excess of a given duration, the ordinates of the resulting direct-runoff hydrograph scale linearly with the volume of excess rainfall, and the time base stays the same regardless of the rainfall's magnitude.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) The theory assumes uniform areal AND temporal distribution of rainfall excess, not arbitrary time variation.
(C) The time base is assumed constant for a given duration, independent of rainfall intensity — this is a core linearity assumption.
(D) Baseflow is separated out before analysis; only direct runoff ordinates are used in unit hydrograph theory.

questions.question: The Reynolds number for flow in a pipe is primarily used to determine:

options.A: Whether the flow regime is laminar or turbulent
options.B: The Darcy friction factor directly, without any further relation
options.C: Whether the fluid is compressible or incompressible
options.D: The total head loss in the pipe directly, without other parameters

questions.solution:
Reynolds number, Re = ρVD/μ, compares inertial to viscous forces and is used to classify pipe flow as laminar (Re < 2000), transitional, or turbulent (Re > 4000).
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Friction factor is obtained from Re via a further relation (e.g., Moody chart or Colebrook equation), not directly equal to Re.
(C) Compressibility is governed by the Mach number, not the Reynolds number.
(D) Head loss requires additional parameters (friction factor, length, diameter, velocity) beyond Re alone.

questions.question: The Plasticity Index (PI) of a soil is defined as:

options.A: Liquid Limit − Plastic Limit
options.B: Liquid Limit + Plastic Limit
options.D: Liquid Limit ÷ Plastic Limit

questions.solution:
Plasticity Index is the range of water content over which the soil remains in a plastic state, defined as PI = LL − PL (Liquid Limit minus Plastic Limit).
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Summing the limits has no physical meaning in Atterberg limit theory.
(C) This mixes the Shrinkage Limit with the Plastic Limit, not the correct pair (LL, PL) that defines PI.
(D) PI is a difference of water contents, not a ratio.

questions.question: In differential (spirit) leveling, a 'back sight' reading is taken on a staff held at a point:

options.A: Of known or previously determined elevation, to establish the height of the instrument
options.B: Of unknown elevation, which the survey is trying to determine
options.C: Only at the very first benchmark of the entire survey
options.D: Only as the last reading taken before closing the survey

questions.solution:
A back sight (BS) is taken on a point of known (or already computed) elevation — such as a benchmark or a turning point — so that the height of instrument (HI) can be calculated as HI = elevation of point + BS reading.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) A reading on a point of unknown elevation, taken to find its elevation, is a fore sight (FS), not a back sight.
(C) Back sights are taken at every instrument setup (at the starting BM and at every turning point), not only at the first benchmark.
(D) The last reading before closing is typically a fore sight onto the closing benchmark, not necessarily a back sight.

questions.question: Field capacity of a soil refers to the soil moisture content at which:

options.A: Gravitational (free) water has drained away and further downward drainage becomes negligible
options.B: All soil pore spaces are completely saturated with water
options.C: Plants can no longer extract any further water from the soil (permanent wilting point)
options.D: Soil moisture tension equals 15 bar

questions.solution:
Field capacity is the moisture content retained by soil (typically at a tension of about 1/3 bar) after gravitational drainage has essentially stopped, generally 2–3 days after saturation and free drainage.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Complete saturation describes the moisture state immediately after irrigation/rainfall, before gravitational drainage occurs — not field capacity.
(C) This describes the permanent wilting point, a different (lower) moisture limit.
(D) 15 bar tension corresponds to the permanent wilting point, not field capacity (~0.33 bar).

questions.question:
An unconfined aquifer has a porosity of 35% and a specific retention of 10%. Calculate the specific yield of the aquifer. (Answer in %.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: %]
questions.solution:
Porosity = Specific yield + Specific retention.
Specific yield = Porosity − Specific retention = 35% − 10% = 25%.

questions.question: Moisture content of a grain sample expressed on a 'wet basis' is defined as the mass of water present, expressed as a percentage of:

options.A: The total mass of the wet sample (water + dry matter)
options.B: The mass of dry matter only
options.D: The mass of the empty sampling container

questions.solution:
Wet-basis moisture content, MCwb (%) = [mass of water / (mass of water + mass of dry matter)] × 100 — i.e., water as a fraction of the total (wet) sample mass. (Dry-basis MC instead divides by dry-matter mass alone.)
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Dividing by dry matter mass alone gives the dry-basis moisture content, not wet-basis.
(C) This would trivially always give 100% and has no practical meaning.
(D) Container mass is not part of the moisture-content definition at all.

questions.question: Rittinger's law for size reduction states that the energy required for size reduction is directly proportional to:

options.A: The new surface area created per unit mass during size reduction
options.B: The size-reduction ratio alone (initial size ÷ final size)
options.D: The logarithm of the size-reduction ratio

questions.solution:
Rittinger's law states E = Kᵣ(1/Df − 1/Di), i.e., energy is proportional to the new surface area generated (inversely related to final particle size Df relative to initial size Di).
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) A simple reduction ratio is not what Rittinger's law uses; it is based on the reciprocal-size (surface area) difference.
(C) Volume reduction is not the basis of Rittinger's surface-area theory.
(D) The logarithmic form of energy vs. reduction ratio describes Kick's law, not Rittinger's law.

questions.question:
A groundnut kernel has approximate mutually perpendicular axial dimensions: length = 15 mm, width = 9 mm, thickness = 7 mm. Calculate its geometric mean diameter, Dg = (L·W·T)^(1/3). (Answer in mm, rounded to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: mm]

A storage bin contains 2400 kg of paddy occupying a bulk volume of 4 m³. Calculate the bulk density of the paddy. (Answer in kg/m³.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: kg/m³]
questions.solution: Bulk density = Mass / Volume = 2400 kg / 4 m³ = 600 kg/m³.

questions.question:
A sample of maize has a moisture content of 25% on a dry basis (MCdb). Calculate the equivalent moisture content on a wet basis (MCwb). (Answer in %, rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: %]
Thermal diffusivity (α) of a food material is defined as:

options.A: α = k / (ρ·Cp)
options.B: α = k × ρ × Cp
options.D: α = Cp / k

questions.solution:
Thermal diffusivity, α = k/(ρCp), where k is thermal conductivity, ρ is density, and Cp is specific heat. It represents how quickly heat diffuses through a material relative to how much heat is stored (thermal capacity) per unit volume.
Why the other options are wrong:
(B) Multiplying instead of dividing by ρCp does not give the physically meaningful diffusivity term.
(C) This omits specific heat entirely and inverts the relationship.
(D) This omits both density and thermal conductivity's role correctly; it is not the definition of diffusivity.

questions.question:
Heat is conducted steadily through a flat slab of a food material of thickness 2 cm and thermal conductivity 0.5 W/(m·K). If the temperature difference across the slab is 20°C, calculate the steady-state heat flux through the slab. (Answer in W/m².)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: W/m²]
questions.solution:
Fourier's law (steady, 1-D conduction): q = k·ΔT/L
q = 0.5 × 20 / 0.02 = 10/0.02 = 500 W/m².

questions.question: A cylindrical farm storage silo, closed at both the top and bottom, must hold a fixed volume V of grain. For the total surface area (and hence the sheet-metal cost) to be minimum, the ratio of the silo's height h to its radius r must equal:
questions.solution:
Surface area S = 2πr² + 2πrh, with V = πr²h fixed ⇒ h = V/(πr²).
S(r) = 2πr² + 2V/r.
dS/dr = 4πr − 2V/r² = 0 ⇒ 4πr³ = 2V ⇒ r³ = V/(2π).
Since V = πr²h, substitute: r³ = πr²h/(2π) = r²h/2 ⇒ r = h/2 ⇒ h/r = 2.
Why the other options are wrong:
(A) Would correspond to a stationary point of a different (non-minimal) cost function.
(C) Results from an algebraic slip when substituting V = πr²h back into r³ = V/(2π).
(D) Results from doubling the correct ratio by mistake.

questions.question:
The larger eigenvalue of the matrix A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]] is ______ (answer as an integer).
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: (dimensionless)]
questions.solution:
Characteristic equation: det(A − λI) = 0.
(4−λ)(3−λ) − (1)(2) = 0
12 − 4λ − 3λ + λ² − 2 = 0
λ² − 7λ + 10 = 0
(λ−5)(λ−2) = 0 ⇒ λ = 5, 2.
The larger eigenvalue is 5.

questions.question:
Evaluate the determinant of the matrix B = [[2, 0, 1], [1, 3, −1], [0, 1, 4]]. (Answer as an integer.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: (dimensionless)]

The germination probability of each seed in a large batch of paddy seeds is 0.8, independent of other seeds. If 5 seeds are sown, find the probability that exactly 4 of them germinate. (Round off to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: (probability, dimensionless)]
questions.solution:
This follows a Binomial distribution: P(X = k) = C(n,k) pᵏ (1−p)^{n−k}, with n = 5, p = 0.8, k = 4.
P(X=4) = C(5,4) × (0.8)⁴ × (0.2)¹ = 5 × 0.4096 × 0.2 = 0.4096 ≈ 0.41.

questions.subtopic: soil tillage and forces on a tillage tool
questions.question:
A single-bottom mouldboard plough operates at a depth of 20 cm and a width of cut of 30 cm. The unit draft (specific soil resistance) of the field soil is 0.5 N/cm². Calculate the draft required by the plough. (Answer in kN, rounded to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: kN]
questions.solution:
Draft = Unit draft × cross-sectional area of cut
Area = depth × width = 20 cm × 30 cm = 600 cm²
Draft = 0.5 N/cm² × 600 cm² = 300 N = 0.30 kN.

questions.subtopic: soil tillage and forces on a tillage tool
questions.question:
A tillage implement requires a draft of 8 kN and is operated at a forward speed of 4 km/h. Calculate the drawbar power required. (Answer in kW, rounded to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: kW]
questions.solution:
Drawbar power P = Draft × forward speed.
Speed = 4 km/h = 4 × 1000/3600 = 1.111 m/s
P = 8000 N × 1.111 m/s = 8888.9 W ≈ 8.89 kW.

questions.question:
A flat-belt drive connects a driving pulley of diameter 250 mm running at 1200 rpm to a driven pulley of diameter 400 mm. Neglecting belt slip, calculate the speed of the driven pulley. (Answer in rpm.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: rpm]
questions.solution:
For a belt drive (no slip): N₁D₁ = N₂D₂
N₂ = N₁D₁/D₂ = (1200 × 250)/400 = 750 rpm.

questions.question:
A boom sprayer has nozzles spaced 0.5 m apart, each discharging 0.8 L/min, and travels at a forward speed of 4 km/h. Calculate the spray application rate. (Answer in L/ha, rounded to the nearest whole number.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: L/ha]
questions.solution:
Application rate (L/ha) = (600 × Q) / (v × s), where Q = nozzle discharge (L/min), v = speed (km/h), s = nozzle spacing (m).
Application rate = (600 × 0.8) / (4 × 0.5) = 480 / 2 = 240 L/ha.

questions.subtopic: traction theory and mechanics of tractor chassis
questions.question:
A tractor weighing 18 kN operates on a firm tilled field where the rolling resistance coefficient is 0.06. The total pull developed at the drive axle is 4.5 kN. Calculate the net drawbar pull available. (Answer in kN, rounded to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: kN]
questions.solution:
Rolling resistance force, Rr = rolling resistance coefficient × tractor weight = 0.06 × 18 = 1.08 kN.
Net drawbar pull = Axle pull − Rolling resistance = 4.5 − 1.08 = 3.42 kN.

questions.subtopic: traction theory and mechanics of tractor chassis
questions.question:
During a field traction test, a tractor's drive wheel makes 40 revolutions while covering a measured distance of 45 m under load (with slip). The same wheel makes 40 revolutions while covering 50 m when operated freely with no load and no slip. Calculate the percentage wheel slip. (Rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: %]
questions.solution:
Percentage slip = [1 − (actual distance travelled under load)/(theoretical distance, no-slip)] × 100
= [1 − 45/50] × 100 = [1 − 0.9] × 100 = 10.0%.

questions.subtopic: engine components and I.C. engine systems
questions.question:
An IC engine cylinder has a swept (displacement) volume of 500 cm³ and a clearance volume of 50 cm³. Calculate the compression ratio of the engine.
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: (dimensionless)]
questions.solution:
Compression ratio, r = (Swept volume + Clearance volume) / Clearance volume
r = (500 + 50)/50 = 550/50 = 11.

questions.topic: Thermodynamic principles and I.C. engine cycles
questions.subtopic: Thermodynamic principles and I.C. engine cycles
questions.question:
An engine operates on the ideal air-standard Otto cycle with a compression ratio of 8. Taking γ = 1.4 for air, calculate the theoretical thermal efficiency of the cycle. (Answer in %, rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: %]

A solar photovoltaic panel of area 2 m² receives solar radiation at 800 W/m² and has an energy conversion efficiency of 15%. Calculate the electrical power output of the panel. (Answer in W.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: W]
questions.solution:
Electrical power output = Incident radiation × Area × Efficiency
= 800 W/m² × 2 m² × 0.15 = 240 W.

questions.question:
A watershed of area 25 hectares has a runoff coefficient of 0.35. Using the Rational Method (Q = CiA/360, with i in mm/h, A in hectares, Q in m³/s), calculate the peak runoff rate for a design rainfall intensity of 60 mm/h. (Answer in m³/s, rounded to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: m³/s]

A rainfall event of 50 mm occurs uniformly over a catchment of area 2 km². If the runoff coefficient is 0.4, calculate the total volume of surface runoff generated. (Answer in m³.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: m³]
questions.solution:
Runoff depth = C × rainfall depth = 0.4 × 50 mm = 20 mm = 0.02 m.
Catchment area = 2 km² = 2 × 10⁶ m².
Runoff volume = 0.02 m × 2 × 10⁶ m² = 40,000 m³.

questions.question:
Water flows through a horizontal pipe that narrows from a diameter of 300 mm to 150 mm. If the mean velocity in the larger section is 1.5 m/s, calculate the velocity in the smaller section using the continuity equation. (Answer in m/s.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: m/s]
questions.solution:
Continuity: A₁V₁ = A₂V₂ ⇒ V₂ = V₁(D₁/D₂)²
V₂ = 1.5 × (300/150)² = 1.5 × 4 = 6.0 m/s.

questions.question:
An irrigation channel with a rectangular cross-section (bed width 2 m, flow depth 1 m) has a bed slope of 0.0004 and Manning's roughness coefficient n = 0.025. Using Manning's equation, calculate the discharge in the channel. (Answer in m³/s, rounded to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: m³/s]

Estimate the average annual soil loss using the Universal Soil Loss Equation (A = R·K·LS·C·P) for a field with: rainfall erosivity R = 350 MJ·mm/(ha·h·yr), soil erodibility K = 0.30 t·ha·h/(ha·MJ·mm), slope-length factor LS = 1.5, cover-management factor C = 0.20, support-practice factor P = 0.5. (Answer in t/ha/yr, rounded to two decimal places.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: t/ha/yr]

A drainage channel cut through silty-clay soil is designed with a mean flow velocity of 0.9 m/s. If the maximum permissible (non-erosive) velocity for this soil is 0.75 m/s, calculate the percentage by which the design velocity exceeds the permissible limit. (Rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: %]
questions.solution:
Percentage excess = [(Design velocity − Permissible velocity)/Permissible velocity] × 100
= [(0.9 − 0.75)/0.75] × 100 = (0.15/0.75) × 100 = 20.0%.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the affinity (similarity) laws for a centrifugal irrigation pump are CORRECT, for a fixed impeller diameter?

options.A: The discharge (Q) of the pump varies directly (linearly) with its rotational speed (N)
options.B: The head (H) developed by the pump varies with the square of its rotational speed (N²)
options.C: The power (P) required by the pump varies with the cube of its rotational speed (N³)
options.D: The risk of cavitation decreases as the pump's suction lift increases

questions.solution:
The centrifugal pump affinity laws (constant impeller diameter) state Q ∝ N, H ∝ N², and P ∝ N³ — statements A, B, and C are all correct restatements of these laws. Statement D is false: a higher suction lift lowers the net positive suction head available, which INCREASES the risk of cavitation, not decreases it.
Why the remaining option(s) are excluded:
(D) Increasing suction lift reduces available NPSH, raising — not lowering — cavitation risk, so this statement is incorrect and must not be selected.

questions.topic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.subtopic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.question:
Water released at the head of an irrigation canal is 500 L/s. Conveyance losses (seepage and evaporation) along the channel amount to 75 L/s. Calculate the water-conveyance efficiency of the canal. (Answer in %, rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: %]
questions.solution:
Conveyance efficiency, Ec = (Water delivered at outlet / Water released at head) × 100
Water delivered = 500 − 75 = 425 L/s
Ec = (425/500) × 100 = 85.0%.

questions.question:
For a subsurface drainage system (Hooghoudt-type steady-state design, drains resting above an impermeable layer), the drain spacing is estimated using S² = (4·K·d·h)/q. Given: hydraulic conductivity K = 0.5 m/day, equivalent depth d = 1.2 m, height of water table above drain level h = 0.6 m, and design drainage coefficient q = 0.01 m/day, calculate the required drain spacing S. (Answer in m.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: m]

A tube well yields a discharge of 15 L/s under a drawdown of 3 m. Calculate the specific capacity of the well. (Answer in L/s per m of drawdown.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: L/s/m]
questions.solution: Specific capacity = Discharge / Drawdown = 15 L/s ÷ 3 m = 5.0 L/s per metre of drawdown.

questions.question: Which of the following factors, if increased while other storage conditions are held constant, will INCREASE the risk of spoilage (mould growth and insect activity) during bulk storage of food grains?

options.A: Grain moisture content
options.B: Storage temperature
options.D: Initial level of insect infestation in the stored grain

questions.solution:
Higher grain moisture content (A) and higher storage temperature (B) both accelerate mould growth, respiration, and insect activity. A higher initial insect infestation load (D) directly increases spoilage risk from the outset. Aeration with cool, dry air (C) is a management practice that LOWERS grain temperature and moisture, reducing — not increasing — spoilage risk, so it must not be selected.
Why the remaining option(s) are excluded:
(C) Cool, dry-air aeration is a corrective/preventive measure that reduces spoilage risk, so it is incorrectly included if selected.

questions.question:
500 kg of wheat at 18% moisture content (wet basis) is to be dried to a safe storage moisture content of 12% (wet basis). Calculate the mass of water that must be removed. (Answer in kg, rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: kg]
questions.solution:
Dry matter is conserved during drying.
Dry matter, Md = Initial mass × (1 − MC1) = 500 × (1 − 0.18) = 500 × 0.82 = 410 kg.
Final wet mass, M2 = Md / (1 − MC2) = 410 / (1 − 0.12) = 410/0.88 = 465.9 kg.
Water removed = M1 − M2 = 500 − 465.9 = 34.1 kg.

questions.question:
Using Rittinger's law, E = Kᵣ(1/Df − 1/Di), the energy required to reduce grain particles from an initial average size of 8 mm to a final size of 2 mm is 12 kJ/kg. Using the same Rittinger's constant Kᵣ, calculate the energy required to further reduce the particles from 2 mm to 1 mm. (Answer in kJ/kg, rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: kJ/kg]

A belt conveyor transporting shelled maize carries material with a cross-sectional area of 0.05 m² on the belt, moving at a belt speed of 1.2 m/s. If the bulk density of shelled maize is 720 kg/m³, calculate the mass flow rate of the conveyor. (Answer in kg/s, rounded to one decimal place.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: kg/s]
questions.solution:
Mass flow rate = Cross-sectional area × Belt speed × Bulk density
= 0.05 m² × 1.2 m/s × 720 kg/m³ = 43.2 kg/s.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about High-Temperature-Short-Time (HTST) pasteurization of milk are CORRECT?

options.A: HTST typically heats milk to about 72°C and holds it for about 15 seconds
options.B: For an equivalent microbial log-reduction, HTST causes less thermal damage to nutrients and flavour than a lower-temperature, longer-time process
options.C: HTST completely sterilizes milk, making it shelf-stable at room temperature without refrigeration
options.D: The microbial lethality of HTST depends on the combined effect of temperature and holding time on microbial death kinetics

questions.solution:
HTST's standard commercial condition is about 72°C for 15 seconds (A). Because higher temperature for a shorter time achieves the same log-reduction with less cumulative heat exposure, it preserves more nutritional/sensory quality than an equivalent low-temperature-long-time process (B). Lethality follows first-order death kinetics, driven jointly by temperature and time (D). Statement C is false: HTST pasteurizes (reduces pathogens/spoilage organisms) but does not sterilize milk — pasteurized milk still requires refrigeration, unlike UHT/sterilized milk.
Why the remaining option(s) are excluded:
(C) HTST milk is not shelf-stable; it still requires refrigerated storage, unlike UHT-sterilized milk.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding evaporative moisture transfer from agricultural produce to surrounding air are CORRECT?

options.A: Mass transfer of moisture from a moist product to the surrounding air occurs due to a vapor-pressure gradient
options.B: Increasing the air velocity around the product generally increases the convective mass-transfer coefficient
options.C: At the equilibrium moisture content, there is no net vapor-pressure gradient between the product and the surrounding air
options.D: The latent heat of vaporization absorbed during evaporative cooling differs across substances solely because of differences in their density

questions.solution:
Moisture moves from the product to the air because the vapor pressure at the product surface exceeds that of the surrounding air (A). Higher air velocity thins the boundary layer, increasing the convective mass-transfer coefficient (B). At equilibrium moisture content, the product's surface vapor pressure equals that of the surrounding air, so the net driving gradient is zero (C). Statement D is incorrect: latent heat of vaporization is governed by intermolecular bonding energy of the substance, not by density alone — this is a spurious causal claim.
Why the remaining option(s) are excluded:
(D) Latent heat of vaporization depends on a substance's molecular/intermolecular properties, not on density alone, so this statement is incorrect.

questions.question:
The decimal reduction time (D-value) of a bacterial spore at a given processing temperature is 2.5 minutes. Calculate the heating time required at that temperature to achieve a 5-log reduction in the spore population. (Answer in minutes.)
[Numerical Answer Type — unit: minutes]
questions.solution:
Thermal death time relation: t = D × (log reduction, n)
t = 2.5 min × 5 = 12.5 minutes.
